title_he: מָה רַבָּה הָאַהֲבָה נִגְלְתָה בַּאֲדֹנֵינוּ הַנַּדִּיב

lines: עַד כִּי בְעָנְיוֹ רָם מַעֲמָדֵנוּ הַשָּׁפֵל
וְהוּא הֵכִין לָנוּ מָדוֹר בְּבֵית הָאָב

review: The hymn is 2 Corinthians 8:9 through to Revelation 5: 2:1–2 is 2 Cor 8:9 (אֲשֶׁר בַּעֲבוּרְכֶם הֶעֱנִי), 3:1–2 John 14:2 with 1 Thess 4:16–17, 4:1–2 1 John 3:2 (נֶחֱזֶהוּ כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא), 5:1–2 Rev 3:21 with 5:8, and 6:1–2 Rev 5:9.

1:2 מִשַּׁחַת שְׁאוֹל — the Arabic مِنْ وَهْدَةِ الْجَحِيم is 'from the pit of hell'; the Hebrew joins שַׁחַת (the psalm's pit, Ps 16:10, לֹא־תִתֵּן חֲסִידְךָ לִרְאוֹת שָׁחַת) to שְׁאוֹל, so the line is the psalm's rescue and not a later description of hell.

2:2 מַעֲמָדֵנוּ הַשָּׁפֵל — the Arabic مَقَامُنَا الدَّنِيّ is 'our low station'; מַעֲמָד is the post-biblical noun for a standing, used here because the line needs an abstract and the biblical עֶמְדָּה occurs only in Mic 1:11. The same noun recurs in hymn 261.

4:1 נֶחֱזֵהוּ … נִהְיֶה כָמֹהוּ — the Arabic نَنْظُرُهُ كَمَا هُوَ نَكُونُ مِثْلَهُ is 1 John 3:2, and the Hebrew keeps the verse's two halves in the same order (vision then likeness), because the stanza's hope depends on seeing first and becoming after.

6:2 זֶמֶר חָדָשׁ — the Arabic تَرْنِيمَةً جَدِيدَةً is the 'new song' of Rev 5:9 and 14:3; the Hebrew uses זֶמֶר, the noun of Ps 81:3 and 1 Chr 16:9, rather than the later שִׁיר חָדָשׁ alone, so the line keeps the cultic singing the vision describes.
